instrument: Patient-Centered Communication Scale for nurses — original South Korean 12-item form
domains: Three original factors: information sharing; patient-as-person; therapeutic alliance. 12 items total; factor-specific item allocations only from approved source.
population: 325 clinical nurses in South Korea, original scale development study.
research_evidence: Joo Y, Jang Y, Park CG, Yang YL. BMC Nursing published 2024-08-13; EFA three factors explaining 59.0%; CFA structure assessed; factor alpha 0.60–0.77; modest reliability for some subscales. Original study 325 nurses.
respondent_languages: KO-KR original development in South Korea; exact original questionnaire language, approved Korean form and English respondent edition not independently established by reviewed evidence. NO independent validated RU or ES forms. FA-IR adaptation is separately indexed PCCS-11, NOT interchangeable.
commercial_digital_permission: Article CC BY 4.0 is not conclusive authorization for reproducing official Korean/English questionnaire, scoring, derivatives and commercial hosted SaaS; confirm direct author/rightsholder grant, third-party source items, official final wording and professional healthcare use restrictions.
verification_status: research_only; original study verified; commercial form/locale and scoring pending
safety_notes: Nurse-rated professional communication skills, not client psychological self-test or a patient-reported outcome; no automated diagnosis, no item text/scoring/cutoffs imported; 12-item three-factor original MUST NOT share 11-item Persian scoring.

instrument: Patient-Centered Communication Scale for nurses — validated Persian 11-item adaptation
domains: Single general patient-centered communication factor (NOT three original subscales). Range 11–55 stated in research but no deployable scoring license.
population: 300 Iranian clinical nurses in Shahroud University-affiliated hospitals, split into independent EFA n150 and CFA n150; single-center hospital nurse population.
research_evidence: Ghasempour S et al., PLOS ONE published 2026-09-18, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0358575; Persian cultural translation with original author Yang's permission for translation/psychometric study; item 4 removed due conceptual overlap with item 5; EFA 1-factor explained 77.78%; alpha/omega >0.70 and ICC >0.80.
respondent_languages: FA-IR: INDEPENDENT verified Persian-language respondent translation and cultural adaptation (11 items; one factor); not identical to original 12-item/three-factor KO-KR version. New validated EN0 RU0 ES0. Back-translated English is NOT independently validated English respondent form.
commercial_digital_permission: Original author approval explicitly covers TRANSLATION AND PSYCHOMETRIC TESTING, not commercial app distribution. PLOS CC BY of paper does not prove commercial hosted respondent wording/scoring rights of parent or translators. Require written SaaS rights from original authors plus Iranian translation authors, approved 11 exact items, scoring and privacy/clinical quality gates.
verification_status: research_only; FA-IR cultural validation verified; commercial app rights pending
safety_notes: Clinician/nurse self-report for communication quality, not patient diagnostic test. No adaptation to general psychotherapy population/clients, no three original subscores, no activation or copied text/scoring; single-center evidence and no measurement invariance across KO/FA.
